name: Tiryakloka - The Animal Realm
description: The realm of primal instinct and predation. The vast ocean depths hold naga courts older than memory and makara that swallow ships whole. Inland, the ancient forest is territory — contested, marked, fought over — while the open meadows are the world's great stage, where khadga charge and bhramara darken the sun. The birds live everywhere, but the high places belong to them alone.

location_names._comment: Tibetan/Sanskrit compound names for animal realm settlements — dens, lairs, watering holes, coral grottos, and sacred gathering sites. Vana/Shing=forest, Jala/Tsho=water/lake, Pakshi/Bya=bird, Mriga=deer/animal, Simha=lion, Naga=serpent, Matsya/Nya=fish, Parvata/Ri=mountain, Aranya=wilderness, Vyaghra=tiger, Gaja=elephant. Suffixes: khar=fort, thang=plain, yul=land, lung=valley, pura=city, gram=village.

zones._comment: Bottom section. Entry zone — player arrives from the Hungry Ghost Realm. Vast coastal shelf and open ocean: deep water channels, coral reef flats, rocky islets, sandy shallows. The naga rule here and they remember everything.
Horizontal wall separating the ocean from the inland zones. A coral barrier ridge — impassable except at tidal passes where the reef breaks. The karka hold these choke-points.

Upper-left section. Dense canopy — dark, layered, territorial. The forest floor is never quiet. Every fallen log is a claim, every fruiting tree a war. The portal to the Human Realm is hidden in the oldest part, near the northwestern corner.
Vertical wall between forest and meadow. A ridgeline of tumbled boulders, thorn scrub, and dry ravines. Hard to cross but not impossible — the passes tend to be where the old game trails are.

Upper-right section. Open sky-brushed plains, termite cathedrals, migration routes, watering holes. Exposure is the currency here — the khadga charge, the yaksha mark territory, the bhramara darken the midday sun. More dangerous than the forest because there is nowhere to hide.

data.description: A shimmering passage rising toward the Human Realm. The oldest trees seem to lean away from it.

pickups.name: Pearl Bed
pickups.message: A cluster of oysters in a quiet reef pocket. Some are worth something.

pickups.name: Driftwood Cache
pickups.message: Someone lashed a waterproof bundle to a root. Long forgotten.

pickups.name: Tidal Pool
pickups.message: A sunlit pool left by the retreating tide. The warmth is almost human.

pickups.name: Coral Shrine
pickups.message: The current makes the offerings sway. Something old is paying attention.

pickups.name: Whale Bone
pickups.message: Whatever lived here was immense. Something useful is lodged in the ribs.

pickups.name: Current Stone
pickups.message: A river of energy runs through the rock. You can feel it in your teeth.

pickups.name: Thermal Vent
pickups.message: Heat pours from a crack in the seafloor. It scours and clarifies.

pickups.name: Drowned Offering
pickups.message: A weighted bundle dropped from above. A prayer, not a cache.

pickups.name: Sunken Cache
pickups.message: A sealed chest — too heavy to float, too good to leave.

pickups.name: Kelp Garden
pickups.message: Dense, living, thriving. It is also edible if you know how.

pickups.name: Naga Altar
pickups.message: Old offerings of gold and mantras pressed into clay.

pickups.name: Entangled Net
pickups.message: Looks like a cache. It is not.

pickups.name: Tide Offering Bowl
pickups.message: Someone filled this at each low tide for a long time.

pickups.name: Deep Water Shimmer
pickups.message: Something luminous rises from below. It passes through you and keeps going.

pickups.name: Sea Cave
pickups.message: Someone used this as a dry stash point during low tide.

events._comment: Flying characters only — kapota waypoint in the crown of a giant strangler fig
events.name: High Canopy Perch

events._comment: Flying characters only — shyena nesting site on a cliff-face above the canopy
events.name: Cliff Aerie

pickups.name: Fallen Log Cache
pickups.message: Something was using this as a pantry. There is food left.

pickups.name: Mushroom Ring
pickups.message: A perfect circle. The smell is medicinal if you know mushrooms.

pickups.name: Wild Beehive
pickups.message: Honey, comb, and propolis. The bees make their feelings known.

pickups.name: Ancient Banyan Roots
pickups.message: The roots are as wide as roads and as old as the forest itself.

pickups.name: River Ford
pickups.message: Shallow, cold, and briefly peaceful.

pickups.name: Territorial Marking
pickups.message: Claw lines cut deep into bark. You study the pattern; it tells you something.

pickups.name: Vanara Stash
pickups.message: Hidden in a tree hollow where no one without nimble fingers could reach. Until now.

pickups.name: Mycelium Bloom
pickups.message: The mycelium puts out a body for one day, then reabsorbs it. You got lucky.

pickups.name: Jungle Spring
pickups.message: Cold and deep and inexhaustible.

pickups.name: Marjara Scratch Post
pickups.message: A tree stripped to white wood by repeated sharpening. The confidence in those marks is unsettling.

pickups.name: Overgrown Offering
pickups.message: Wrapped in vines now, but still intact. Whatever was asked for here, it was asked sincerely.

pickups.name: Deadfall Trap
pickups.message: Looks safe. It is a deadfall trap.

pickups.name: Forest Cache
pickups.message: A waterproofed bundle wedged in a root fork, deliberately hidden.

pickups.name: Scattered Feathers
pickups.message: Something large came down here. The feathers say a raptor. The silence says it won.

pickups.name: Storm-Felled Tree
pickups.message: The fall tore open a dry rot cavity. Usable material inside.

events._comment: Flying characters only — uluka oracle perched on an isolated cliff stack
events.name: Cliff Oracle

events._comment: Flying characters only — high thermal column used by raptors and kapota alike
events.name: Thermal Column

pickups.name: Termite Mound
pickups.message: Rich in resin and edible material. The builders disagree.

pickups.name: Old Game Trail Cache
pickups.message: Buried where the trail bends, marked with a chipped stone.

pickups.name: Watering Hole
pickups.message: Shared by everyone and fought over at dusk. Right now it is quiet.

pickups.name: Yaksha Standing Stone
pickups.message: Marked with a boundary script no living scholar recognizes. You touch it anyway.

pickups.name: Dura Earth Cache
pickups.message: Packed into a ceramic vessel and buried with deliberate care.

pickups.name: Scattered Bones
pickups.message: A khadga died here. Something useful remains.

pickups.name: Bhramara Comb
pickups.message: An abandoned section of hive, thick with resin and old honey.

pickups.name: Patanga Silk Cache
pickups.message: The silk is strong and worth something to the right buyer.

pickups.name: Wind-Carved Rock
pickups.message: The stone has been reading the wind for a thousand years. Something of that patience transfers.

pickups.name: Sacred Anthill
pickups.message: Every pilgrim tradition in the meadow passes through here. They all leave something.

pickups.name: Khadga Wallow
pickups.message: A great mud depression, still warm. Restorative in a basic way.

pickups.name: Grassfire Remains
pickups.message: The fire passed through fast and left useful debris behind.

pickups.name: Broken Yaksha Idol
pickups.message: Toppled, old, still radiating something. May be blessing. May be warning.

pickups.name: Grazing Ground
pickups.message: Rich vegetation, undisturbed. Whoever grazed here is gone for now.

pickups.name: Storm-Cleared Field
pickups.message: A lightning strike burned a circle in the grass. The soil underneath is charged.
